harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 as a persistent, read-only TFTP server for the approved boot tree. Node2 downloads both approved files with matching hashes; uploads, overwrites, and traversal outside the boot root are rejected. Both nodes were restarted sequentially and fully recovered with changed boot identities.
actions_performed: Installed the CentOS Stream 10 distribution-provided tftp-server package without changing the OS release or kernel.
Set /srv/legacy2/tftp-firmware-distribution/boot as the secure TFTP root.
Applied persistent SELinux labels, non-writable permissions, systemd read-only hardening, and a node2-scoped firewall rule.
Configured node2 connection tracking for TFTP data-channel replies.
Verified approved downloads, byte-preserving firmware transfer, upload rejection, overwrite rejection, and path-traversal rejection.
Restarted node1 and node2 individually and verified post-restart recovery.

evidence.requirement: Publish only the approved boot tree as a read-only TFTP root
evidence.summary: Effective service configuration uses the boot directory as its secure root; permissions, SELinux labels, hardening, UDP/69 listener, and firewall scope are shown before and after restart.

evidence.requirement: Node2 can download boot.cfg and firmware.bin with firmware bytes preserved
evidence.summary: Both files downloaded successfully before and after restarts; SHA-256 hashes match the staged source hashes.

evidence.requirement: Uploads, overwrites, and requests outside the boot root are rejected
evidence.summary: TFTP rejected new-file creation, approved-file overwrite, and ../private traversal. No unauthorized files appeared and approved source hashes remained unchanged.

evidence.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use compatible software
evidence.summary: The distribution-provided tftp-server 5.2-51.el10 was installed; final state remains CentOS Stream 10 with kernel 6.12.0-205.el10.x86_64.
Boot ID changed from 0581c914-b77e-45ce-b511-c0c9f578a303 to e8a10c02-4722-46ca-83a6-12b91191be20. The TFTP socket, security state, data hashes, and end-to-end downloads recovered.

Boot ID changed from 96974ac3-f19e-45f7-9672-e880dd505cf8 to 2787fc4b-d54f-4eed-b702-3df946b23e60. Firewalld and the TFTP helper recovered, approved downloads matched, and rejection controls remained effective.
